judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Content Standards in Strand 1: Number (same statement-type grain, same rank 2), but in different Sub-Strands: B6.1.1.1 covers quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals up to 1 billion (Sub-Strand 1: Counting, Representation, Cardinality & Ordinality), while B6.1.2.2 covers multiplication of a 2 or 3-digit number by a 2 or 3-digit number (Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations). The relation is substantive rather than merely lexical: secure understanding of multi-digit place value and quantity magnitude underpins multi-digit multiplication procedures (partial products, regrouping, positional alignment, reasonableness of products), so proficiency in the place-value standard supports success in the multiplication standard. Same-rank direction is justified by this operational dependency of number operations on place-value understanding, not by code order or shared ancestry. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (34 and 24 omitted source-evidence items) and no Learning Components were supplied, which limits confirmation of explicit place-value usage inside the multiplication indicators.

First (B5.1.4.1.5) is modelling the product of a decimal (to thousandths) by a whole number under the decimal-fractions standard; second (B5.1.5.1.2) is deriving benchmark percentages from common fractions and using them to estimate percentages of quantities under the percentage standard. They cohere substantively as complementary work on equivalent rational-number representations (decimals, common fractions, percentages) and on operating on quantities, so meaningful reinforcement is supported. However, neither indicator's bounded text shows the other's proficiency as a support for its success: benchmark-percentage estimation is framed on common fractions rather than decimal multiplication, and the modelling indicator does not extend to percentage estimation. With equal rank, no substantive evidence justifies a developmental direction, so the symmetric relation is chosen.
